title: Monitoring AI Use by Primary School Students
what_it_is: Monitoring AI Use by Primary School Students

sections.label: Questions on AI in primary education
sections.summary: Questions ask the Education Minister about prerequisites, the Primary 4 entry point, implementation roadmap, teacher support, safeguards, and rollout assessment for AI in primary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what prerequisite skills must primary school students demonstrate before AI is first introduced for usage; (b) what is the rationale for the Primary 4 entry point; (c) what is the implementation roadmap for AI in primary curricula, including age cohorts and approved tools; and (d) what guidelines, training and workload support will teachers receive to distinguish productive AI use from shortcut substitution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in respect of the use of artificial intelligence in education (a) whether the Ministry has established safeguards to ensure (i) transparency to parents on data collected through AI-enabled learning tools and (ii) procedural fairness when students are penalised for inappropriate AI use; and (b) if so, what do these safeguards entail.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what does the introduction of AI from Primary 4 under "low exposure" and close teacher supervision entail, including whether it refers only to curated MOE- and GovTech-developed tools in the Student Learning Space; (b) why Primary 4 is chosen as the starting point; and (c) how the Ministry will assess readiness for any broader rollout of AI tools in schools.

sections.label: MOE approach to AI
sections.summary: MOE's approach is for every student to learn about AI, learn to use AI, learn with AI and learn beyond AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education's (MOE’s) approach is simple, but deliberate – for every student to learn about AI, learn to use AI, learn with AI and most importantly, learn beyond AI.

sections.label: AI literacy in Primary 1 to 3
sections.summary: From Primary 1 to 3, hands-on learning is prioritised and students learn AI basics but are not assigned work requiring direct AI use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: From Primary 1 to 3, physical, tactile, hands-on learning is prioritised as students build foundational knowledge and develop cognitive and social skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But students learn about the basics of AI – so, AI literacy – so that they are aware of its presence in their daily lives, but schools will not assign any work that requires them to use AI directly.

sections.label: Code for Fun from Primary 4
sections.summary: From Primary 4, students undergo the mandatory 10-hour Code for Fun programme, with optional five-hour AI for Fun modules on generative AI and computer vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: From Primary 4, students undergo the mandatory 10 hours "Code for Fun" programme – it is coding for fun, but it is mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Under Code for Fun, primary schools can also opt for two additional "AI for Fun" modules, each five hours, that delve further into generative AI and computer vision respectively.

sections.label: AI prohibited in national exams
sections.summary: National exams continue to be proctored and the use of AI is prohibited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: National exams continue to be proctored and use of AI is prohibited.

sections.label: Anonymised data from MOE AI tools
sections.summary: Data from students' use of MOE-built AI tools is anonymised and not used to train external AI models powering these tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Besides the educational guardrails to ensure good learning, Data from students’ use of MOE-built AI tools is anonymised and not used to train external AI models that power these tools.

sections.label: SG-LEADS children AI usage study
sections.summary: A*STAR's SG-LEADS study will start collecting data in 2027 to understand Singapore children's AI usage patterns and effects on learning and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One example is the Singapore Longitudinal Early Development Study (SG-LEADS) by the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), which will start to collect data in 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This research seeks to understand Singapore children’s AI usage patterns and how their AI usage affects their learning and well-being outcomes.

sections.label: AI in education guiding principles
sections.summary: The approach to AI in education has two guiding principles: students at the centre, and pedagogy first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And our approach is one that — I have brought this document for everybody to take a look.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is our approach to AI in education and we have, as a guiding principle, number one, students at the centre: "keeping student learning as the goal and maintaining student agency".

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And principle number two is pedagogy first, which means "good teaching and learning must come first, enabled by skillful use of AI".

sections.label: AI not for social emotional learning
sections.summary: For children from more vulnerable families, AI in education, SLS and MOE schools is not used for affective or social emotional issues or learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Likewise, for children coming from more vulnerable families – AI in education, AI in SLS, AI in MOE schools is not used for affective or social emotional issues or social emotional learning.

sections.label: Sweden reversing digitalisation strategy
sections.summary: The conclusion drew on peer-reviewed studies, and Sweden reversed its digitalisation strategy in 2023, investing over €200 million to reintroduce physical textbooks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That conclusion drew on multiple peer-reviewed studies covering reading comprehension, distraction, executive function development and equity outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And the Swedish government acted on this, reversing its digitalisation strategy in 2023 and investing over €200 million to reintroduce physical textbooks and removing mandatory digital tools for young children.

sections.label: Avoiding cognitive offload with AI
sections.summary: MOE tools in SLS are teacher-supervised and structured so children cannot ask for spoon-fed answers, preventing cognitive offload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I think on the first point, we are ad idem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We want to make sure that in using AI tools, our children do not cognitively offload – and that is shorthand for saying that they rely on the AI as a crutch to deliver the answer, but not learn deeply, so they do not develop cognitively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And that is why in my earlier reply, I mentioned that the MOE tools that are used in SLS are teacher-supervised and the tools are structured in a way that they do not allow children to ask for spoon-fed answers.

sections.label: Guarding against general purpose AI
sections.summary: SLS teaching uses AI tools for an educative purpose, but children must be guarded against general purpose AI tools outside this environment causing cognitive offload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In our teaching approaches through SLS, we have used the AI tools for an educative purpose, but we need to guard against children using general purpose AI tools outside this teaching environment, which may cause them to cognitively offload.

sections.label: AI literacy from young
sections.summary: Starting AI literacy young, with teacher and parent supervision, gives children principles for independent use later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: You cannot switch it off; in some instances, in your general search tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And it is far better to start AI literacy young and start getting our kids to use AI for learning in a highly scaffolded teacher supervised and of course, parents supervised way, and then as they grow older, when they start using these tools independently, that they have the principles and foundation to be able to build on it.

sections.label: Age restrictions on tools
sections.summary: Tools with age restrictions will not be used for children below that age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If the tool has an age restriction, then we will not use it for children below that age.
Let us take it back to see how we can do it in a meaningful way and scalable manner.

sections.label: Support for less privileged children
sections.summary: Less privileged children lack home scaffolding, addressed through MOE Opportunity Fund, ComLink, Gift-A-Family and community partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is about the children in less privileged backgrounds not having the same amount of scaffolding and support at home and outside school on a whole range of issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have different approaches to handling that – the MOE Opportunity Fund, we have ComLink, we have Gift-A-Family, we have many other schemes that involve deep partnership with the community.

sections.label: AI age-based safeguards question
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOE will recommend age-based guidelines and safeguards to MDDI for AI tools, especially standalone ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Given MOE's position that AI exposure in schools currently begins from Primary 4 under low exposure and close teacher supervision, my question to the Minister is whether MOE has been consulted or will consider providing recommendations to the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI), as it studies the AI nutrition label and online safeguards, particularly whether AI tools, especially standalone AI tools, should have age-based guidelines, safeguards or default protect protections that apply differently for younger children?

sections.label: AI literacy from Primary 1
sections.summary: AI tools are used in SLS under supervision from Primary 4, but AI literacy starts from Primary 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, while we start using AI for learning and allow our children to use AI tools in SLS under supervision from Primary 4, but for AI literacy from MOE's perspective, we start from Primary 1.

sections.label: NotebookLM for upper secondary
sections.summary: NotebookLM is available to upper secondary students through iCON, and its usage is being monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Of course, we have, through iCON for upper secondary school students, NotebookLM, which is available to upper secondary school students and for which we are monitoring its usage.
